title: Tech Note: Authenticating Web Service Requests

historical_commentary.text: This note explains the three common ways 4th Dimension 2004 supported passing authentication credentials with an outbound SOAP web service call — HTTP Basic auth via AUTHENTICATE WEB SERVICE, SOAP header values via SET WEB SERVICE OPTION, and standard SOAP input parameters via SET WEB SERVICE PARAMETER — since the SOAP 1.1/1.2 standards themselves left authentication undefined and every provider handled it differently. SOAP-based web services and their associated authentication conventions have become largely obsolete as the industry moved to REST/JSON APIs with standardized auth schemes like OAuth and API keys, making this note's specific guidance primarily of historical interest today.
related_updates: SOAP web services have been broadly superseded by REST/JSON APIs across the industry
Modern web service authentication typically uses OAuth, API keys, or bearer tokens rather than the SOAP-header/HTTP-Basic techniques described here
4D's HTTP Client commands and REST-based integration approaches have superseded native SOAP-calling commands like AUTHENTICATE WEB SERVICE for most current use cases
